title: Private Observability Min Pack - Working Spec (Draft)
content:
Working spec / scratchpad for: “Private observability minimum pack”

Owner: Sergio (dashboards/alerts). PM DRI: Vivek. Program: Talia.
Last edited: 2025-02-12

NOTE: This doc is intentionally rough. Confluence will be the canonical operator docs once we settle supported components + config knobs.

---

1) Problem statement (from installs + support)

Private (VPC + on-prem) installs regularly go live without:
- usable latency/error dashboards on day 1
- clear “is this supported?” criteria
- consistent alerting (either nothing pages, or everything pages)
- reliable log forwarding defaults (drops, huge volume, unclear field schema)

Support symptoms we keep seeing:
- SUP-2419: “no clear latency dashboards / baseline panels”
- SUP-2427: on-prem log forwarding to SIEM drops events / backlog
- SUP-2431: alert rules not loading post-upgrade (promtool errors)
- INT-1184: Grafana provisioning failing due to RBAC
- Incidents drill thread: rules failed to fire due to rule loading issues (Slack #incidents 1708977729)

Goal: ship a baseline pack that is “day-1 usable” and reduces bespoke work.

Non-goals (explicit):
- not building a new observability backend
- not doing customer-specific bespoke dashboards beyond the baseline
- not long-retention analytics (Console/Telemetry roadmap)

---

2) Definition of “Minimum Pack” (draft)

Pack = versioned bundle integrated into Private installer / Helm charts containing:
A) Dashboards (Grafana JSON + provisioning)
B) Alert rules (PrometheusRule groups) + defaults for routing (customer-managed Alertmanager)
C) Log pipeline defaults (collector configs + structured schema expectations)
D) Validation harness (“are required signals present?”)
E) Operator docs + runbooks

Operating principle:
- same signals across hosted/dedicated/private where possible
- minimal external dependencies
- safe by default (no secrets, default RBAC, TLS guidance)
- cardinality-aware metrics contract

“Supported” should mean:
- Redwood can reproduce an environment with these components
- Redwood dashboards + alert rules load without modification
- required signals are present, within cardinality bounds
- baseline runbooks map to the dashboards/alerts customers have

---

3) Scope (what’s included)

Dashboards (initial list):
1. Gateway / API Overview
   - RPS, p50/p95/p99 latency (prefill/total), errors (4xx vs 5xx), streaming disconnect rate
   - Top routes/models by volume and error rate
   - Request size distribution (input tokens), output tokens, throttles/rate limit hits (if applicable)

2. Runtime Performance
   - prefill latency vs decode latency
   - queue depth / queue wait time (saturation)
   - batch size distribution
   - KV cache hit rate (if enabled)
   - OOM / CUDA errors (from logs + counters)

3. GPU Saturation
   - util, mem, throttling, temperature (if exported)
   - correlation panels: GPU util vs p95 latency, vs error rate

4. Routing / Fallback Behavior (Private-specific)
   - fallback rate by policy/model
   - “capacity constrained” rejects
   - cross-region routing count (only if enabled)

5. Control Plane Health
   - auth integration health (OIDC / SAML connectors if relevant)
   - config/policy store health (latency, error rate)
   - rollout controller status

6. Installer / Upgrade Health
   - installer job status, step durations
   - chart/pack version pinned
   - last successful reconciliation timestamp

Alert groups (initial list):
- Availability + latency SLO (burn-rate) for gateway
- High error rate (5xx) immediate
- Queue buildup / saturation (runtime queue depth / queue wait)
- GPU resource exhaustion / OOM risk indicators
- Log pipeline health (collector drops/backlog/export failures)
- Missing signals (dashboard prerequisites missing for >N minutes)
- Rule loading health (Prometheus rules failing to load / parse)

Log pipeline defaults:
- collectors: choose 1-2 supported agents (Vector + Fluent Bit are the frontrunners)
- structured logs from: gateway, runtime, control plane, installer
- redaction defaults: never log prompt text by default in Private (unless explicitly enabled). Always redact auth tokens.

Validation:
- post-install command in installer: checks metrics endpoints, Grafana API reachability, Prom rules loaded, sample queries return series
- “Supported signals” report output (ENG-2852)

---

4) Supported components (comparison + open decision)

We need a crisp support matrix that works for VPC and on-prem/air-gapped.

Metrics + alerting:
Option A: Prometheus Operator (kube-prometheus-stack)
- Pros: common in customer clusters, easy PrometheusRule CRDs, lots of existing tooling.
- Cons: version skew; air-gapped upgrades can be painful; some customers refuse operator-managed monitoring.

Option B: Plain Prometheus (no operator)
- Pros: minimal footprint, fewer CRDs.
- Cons: harder packaging for rule distribution; customers need to wire rule files manually.

Draft direction (not final):
- Support PrometheusRule format primarily (Operator / VictoriaMetrics operator compatible), but provide an export path to raw rule files.
- Customer owns Alertmanager routing; we provide recommended receiver/severity mapping.

Dashboards:
Option A: Grafana provisioning (folders/datasources/dashboards via ConfigMaps/sidecar)
- Pros: “it just appears”; good day-1 experience.
- Cons: RBAC and auth defaults are sensitive; collisions with existing Grafana; audit logging considerations.

Option B: “Import JSON” only
- Pros: minimal privileges.
- Cons: high friction; not day-1 friendly; inconsistent installs.

Draft direction:
- Provide provisioning hooks where Redwood installs Grafana (or when customer opts into Redwood-managed Grafana).
- Provide import/export support for customer-managed Grafana (manual steps + API token-based import).

Logs:
Option A: Fluent Bit
- Pros: ubiquitous; lots of output plugins.
- Cons: config can get hairy; transforms less ergonomic.

Option B: Vector
- Pros: strong transforms, good for schema enforcement + sampling.
- Cons: less common in some enterprise environments; might be “one more thing.”

Forwarding targets we should explicitly support:
- customer SIEM via syslog / HTTP collector endpoint
- object storage (S3-compatible) for bulk logs (when SIEM is too expensive)
- “existing customer log backend” (Splunk HEC, Elastic, etc.) via agent outputs

Open question: do we officially support a log backend like Loki?
- If yes, we become responsible for scaling + retention tuning guidance.
- If no, we must ensure the experience still feels complete (dashboards might need Loki queries; avoid those).

Draft stance (as of 2025-02-12):
- The min pack should NOT require Loki.
- Dashboards should rely on metrics; logs are for drill-down and SIEM export.

Tracing:
- Nice-to-have for the “minimum pack,” but might be too much for air-gapped.
- Proposal: define OTLP integration points (customer-managed collector) but do not ship tracing infra in min pack.

Security/audit:
- Grafana: access logs + admin actions should be auditable.
- Prometheus: rule changes should be tracked (at least via GitOps change control in docs).
- Collectors: ensure TLS to SIEM endpoints; avoid plaintext credentials in ConfigMaps.

Action item: capture final decisions in ADR (thread: Slack #architecture 1708689913).

---

5) Metrics + labels contract (sketch)

We need stable metric names + labels across private.

Must-have labels (draft):
- tenant (or tenant_id) — BUT must have controlled cardinality (bounded tenants)
- model
- route (or endpoint)
- region/cluster (private cluster identifier)

Cardinality guardrails:
- do not label on request_id
- do not label on full error strings
- restrict “route” to configured route names (not arbitrary URLs)

Metrics we think we need (names TBD, aligned with Platform/Telemetry):
- gateway_request_total{route,model,tenant,status_class}
- gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route,model,tenant}
- runtime_prefill_duration_seconds_bucket{model,tenant}
- runtime_decode_tokens_total{model,tenant}
- runtime_queue_depth{model}
- runtime_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{model}
- runtime_batch_size_bucket{model}
- runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{model} (if enabled)
- controlplane_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service,operation}
- installer_reconcile_success{component}

Open questions for Nadia/Logan:
- which label key names are “blessed” (tenant vs org vs workspace)
- do we expose “deployment_mode” label (vpc/onprem) or keep it external

Linked work:
- ENG-2845 (metrics contract) + redwood PR #28741 (emit missing labels + cardinality guardrails)

---

6) Dashboard sketches (very rough)

6.1 Gateway Overview dashboard panels
- Stat: RPS (1m)
- Graph: request latency p50/p95/p99 (5m), split by route (templated variable)
- Graph: 4xx rate, 5xx rate (stacked)
- Table: top 10 routes by error rate
- Graph: streaming disconnects / client cancel
- Heatmap: request duration distribution

Variables:
- cluster
- tenant
- model
- route

Notes:
- avoid panels that require logs
- avoid “top N by label” queries if they explode cardinality (needs careful query design)

6.2 Runtime Perf dashboard panels
- Prefill latency p50/p95
- Decode latency per token (approx) or decode token throughput
- Queue depth + queue wait
- Batch size histogram (if available)
- KV cache hit ratio + eviction rate

6.3 GPU dashboard panels
- GPU util per node
- GPU mem used
- GPU throttling / power limit (if we can export reliably)
- Correlation: GPU util vs p95 latency

6.4 Installer/Upgrade dashboard panels
- “Pack install status” (last run, last success)
- “Rule load status” (count of loaded rule groups)
- “Grafana provisioning status” (API reachable + folder exists)

---

7) Alerting philosophy (draft notes for SRE review)

We need to be explicit on:
- what pages vs what tickets
- how to tune for customer workloads

Draft severity mapping:
- SEV0 / Page: hard outage, severe SLO burn, rule/pipeline broken (we’re blind)
- SEV1 / Page (business hours or depending on customer): sustained latency degradation, high 5xx
- SEV2 / Ticket: capacity approaching limits, increased fallback rate, rising queue

SLO burn-rate:
- We should use standard multi-window burn alerts (ex: 5m/1h and 30m/6h pairs)
- Need to define the default SLO targets for Private (availability and latency)

Potential default SLOs (placeholders; need Sean/Allison sign-off):
- Gateway availability: 99.9% (5xx and network failures)
- Gateway latency: p95 < X ms (this is dangerous as a global default; might need “relative to baseline” guidance)

Open question: latency SLO as absolute vs per-model/per-route.
- Absolute is too noisy across model sizes.
- Alternative: only alert on “latency regression vs last 1h baseline” (but harder to reason about).

Immediate alerts (non-SLO):
- 5xx spike above threshold
- rule loading failure / promtool parse failure
- log collector dropping >N% events
- missing metrics series for golden signals

References:
- SRE review thread: Slack #eng-sre 1708451122
- Alert noise review will land in a separate sheet/doc (ENG-2860)

---

8) Packaging and deployment constraints (esp. on-prem/air-gapped)

Constraints we must respect:
- some on-prem clusters have zero egress
- customers may require mirrored images + offline chart bundles
- customers may already run Prometheus/Grafana and will not allow Redwood to install them

Packaging needs:
- a single “observability pack” artifact versioned and pinned by Private installer
- optional offline bundle: dashboards + rules + collector configs + container images (if we ship any collectors)

Open question: do we ship collectors as part of pack?
- Shipping collectors increases scope (images, CVEs, upgrades)
- Not shipping collectors reduces day-1 reliability (“you’re on your own”)

Draft approach:
- For VPC reference: ship collectors (opt-out)
- For strict on-prem: provide collector manifests + config templates, but allow “bring your own agent” mode

Related thread: Slack #eng-infra 1708612255
Related work: ENG-2846 + installer PR #909 (air-gapped bundle input)

---

9) Validation / “supported signals” checklist (what we should automate)

We need a deterministic pass/fail checklist used by Solutions + SRE during go-live.

Validation checks (draft):
- Prometheus reachable and scraping Redwood targets
- Required metrics exist (series count > 0 for last 10m)
- Grafana reachable; folder exists; N dashboards provisioned
- Prometheus rules loaded successfully (no parse errors); expected rule groups present
- Log collector running (if installed) and export success counter increasing

Output:
- human-readable report + JSON for attachment to tickets
- include versions: private-installer version, pack version, chart version

Linked work:
- installer PR #908 (post-install validation)
- ENG-2852 (installer report)

---

10) Open questions / decisions needed

(1) Supported backend matrix (must decide for GA)
- Prometheus Operator required vs optional?
- Grafana provisioning required vs optional?
- Log agent choice: Vector vs Fluent Bit (supporting both might be too heavy)

(2) Do we ship Grafana?
- Redwood-managed Grafana improves experience but increases security/compliance burden.
- If customers bring Grafana, we need a clean “import/provisioning API” path.

(3) How do we handle multi-tenant/private clusters?
- label schema must be stable; cardinality controls must be enforced

(4) Alert defaults for latency
- absolute thresholds are risky; we need a safe default that doesn’t page constantly

(5) Logging: prompt/response content
- default: DO NOT log prompts/responses
- provide explicit opt-in with warnings + sampling

(6) Audit logging requirements
- what evidence do regulated customers need around:
  - Grafana access
  - dashboard edits
  - alert rule changes

Owner list for decisions:
- Supported matrix: Vivek + Allison + Sean
- Metrics contract naming: Nadia + Logan
- On-prem packaging: Fatima + Bruno
- Audit/security: Naomi + Marcus + Kevin

---

11) Risks / gotchas

- Metrics cardinality blowups if we include route/model/tenant labels without guardrails.
- Grafana provisioning failures (RBAC) can make dashboards “disappear” silently.
- Prometheus version skew => rule syntax issues (SUP-2431 class). Need CI tests + promtool validation.
- On-prem log forwarding can overload SIEM or drop events; we need sampling and “drop counters” instrumentation.
- Customers with pre-existing monitoring stacks will resist Redwood-managed components; need clean integration story.

---

12) Next steps (near-term)

- Finalize component support via ADR (target: end of Discovery phase)
- Lock metrics + label contract (ENG-2845)
- Prototype 2-3 core dashboards end-to-end + provisioning (ENG-2842, PR #318/#319)
- Implement baseline PrometheusRule bundle + CI validation (ENG-2843, PR #322/#323)
- Draft operator install guide outline in parallel (Elliot)
- Run “incident drill” in staging with the pack enabled (validate that alerts fire and dashboards are usable)

---

Appendix B: Notes to self (parking lot)
- We should add a “Read me first” dashboard tab with links to runbooks.
- Consider a single “Golden signals” dashboard first (availability/latency/errors/saturation) before splitting by component.
- Remember to include “quota / throttling” panels if Private exposes those controls.
- Ensure we have an alert for “we are blind” (missing scrape targets / exporter down) that is distinct from actual service outage.
